h1: LCSW Therapist in Memphis: Virtual Support for Adults
meta_description: Find virtual therapy and coaching for adults in Memphis and Tennessee. Support for stress, burnout, and life transitions with Hicks Consulting.
direct_answer: An LCSW therapist in Memphis is a Licensed Clinical Social Worker who provides mental health services to individuals in the local community. These professionals help adults manage stress, anxiety, and life transitions. Hicks Consulting offers virtual individual therapy and coaching to residents in Memphis and across Tennessee through a secure online platform.

sections.heading: How does virtual therapy work in Memphis?
paragraphs: Virtual therapy allows you to meet with a licensed professional from your own space. Hicks Consulting provides all services online. There are no physical office visits. This format serves adults living in Memphis neighborhoods like Whitehaven, Hickory Hill, and Midtown. You might be familiar with the commute along Poplar Avenue or I-240. Online sessions remove the need to drive through local traffic. You must be physically located in the state of Tennessee during your session to receive therapy. This model is helpful for Black women managing busy schedules, family needs, or workplace stress. Reading this information is not therapy. If you are in a crisis, please call or text 988 immediately. Virtual care is a grounded way to address burnout and relationship strain without leaving your home. It offers a private environment for those seeking a professional who understands the local culture and challenges of living in the Mid-South.

sections.heading: What services are available for Memphis residents?
paragraphs: Hicks Consulting offers several paths for personal and professional growth. Each service is tailored to the needs of the individual or organization. For those seeking clinical support, virtual individual therapy is available for adults in Tennessee. If you are looking for guidance that is not clinical, virtual coaching is an option. Support groups are also available for those who find comfort in shared experiences. For local businesses and groups, organizational mental health training and speaking services are offered. Consulting is another way to address workplace wellness. Some clients prefer to include their spiritual beliefs in their sessions. A Christian, faith-integrated approach is available in therapy or coaching when the client wants it. This is never imposed on anyone. You can learn more by viewing Memphis Mental Health Providers Compared | Hicks Consulting or reading about being a Black Therapist in Memphis | Hicks Consulting.

sections.heading: Is therapy, coaching, or a group right for you?
paragraphs: Choosing the right type of support depends on your current needs. Therapy often focuses on clinical concerns like anxiety or deep-seated relationship strain. It is a regulated health service provided by a Licensed Clinical Social Worker. Coaching is non-clinical and focuses on specific life goals or professional transitions. It does not involve a diagnosis or clinical treatment. Support groups offer a community setting to discuss common stressors. Many Black women in Memphis find that a gender-specific environment feels more comfortable. You can explore this further in Female Therapists in Memphis: Gender Fit | Hicks Consulting. Employers in the Memphis area also seek training to help their teams manage burnout. These sessions provide tools for the workplace. Whether you are navigating a career change or personal stress, there is a format that fits your situation. All services are conducted online for your convenience.

sections.heading: Local Memphis Resources and Crisis Support
paragraphs: Memphis has several resources for those needing immediate or community-based support. The 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline is available 24/7 for anyone in distress. Locally, the Memphis Police Department works with CIT officers for mental health emergencies. Shelby County residents can also access the Tennessee Statewide Crisis Line. For community-level support, the Memphis Crisis Center provides a local touchpoint for those in need. It is important to know that Hicks Consulting is not a crisis service. Online therapy and coaching are scheduled appointments. If you are near landmarks like the National Civil Rights Museum or the Liberty Bowl and find yourself in an emergency, please use the local crisis numbers or go to the nearest emergency room. Staying connected to local resources ensures you have a safety net while you pursue long-term support through virtual therapy or coaching.

faq.q: Can I see a therapist in person at Hicks Consulting?
faq.a: No. All services at Hicks Consulting are virtual only. There are no office visits. You must be located in Tennessee during your online session. This allows for flexible scheduling and removes the need for a commute within Memphis.

faq.q: What is the difference between therapy and coaching?
faq.a: Therapy is a clinical service provided by a licensed professional to address mental health conditions. Coaching is non-clinical and focuses on personal or professional goals. Hicks Consulting offers both options virtually to adults in Tennessee based on their specific needs.

faq.q: Is faith included in the therapy sessions?
faq.a: A Christian, faith-integrated approach is available only if the client prefers it. It is never imposed. The therapist is a Licensed Clinical Social Worker and does not claim pastoral or denominational credentials. This integration is entirely optional for the client.

faq.q: Does Hicks Consulting work with Memphis employers?
faq.a: Yes. Hicks Consulting provides organizational mental health training and speaking services. These are designed for workplaces looking to support their staff. Consulting services are also available to help organizations improve their approach to mental health and wellness.
